text: Tom wanted to mend the boat before the tide came in. The boat sank.
note: control: lexicon happens to agree here (sank is UNMET-lexicon and gold is UNMET)

text: Tom wanted the boat to sink so he could collect the insurance money. The boat sank.
note: flip: sank is unconditionally UNMET in the lexicon regardless of whose goal it serves; gold is MET because sinking WAS the goal

text: Nora wanted to save the old oak tree from the storm. The tree fell.
note: control: lexicon happens to agree here

text: Nora wanted the old oak tree to fall so she could clear the lot for a shed. The tree fell.
note: flip: same failure mode as A-met, verb 'fell'

text: Kate wanted to win the chess tournament. Kate lost the final match.
note: control: lexicon happens to agree here

text: Kate wanted her rival to lose the final match. Kate's rival lost the final match.
note: flip: same failure mode as A-met/B-met, verb 'lost'; also tests referent binding (rival, not Kate herself)

text: Owen wanted to win the race. Owen won the race.
note: control: non-flip, lexicon agrees

text: Owen wanted his sister to win the race. Owen's rival won the race.
note: entity-binding stress: won is unconditionally MET in the lexicon regardless of WHO won; gold is UNMET because the actual referent (rival) does not match the desired referent (sister)

text: Liam wanted to open the vault before the alarm sounded. The vault shut.
note: new-family control (OPEN_CLASS/CLOSE_CLASS): lexicon is OOV on 'shut'/'vault' entirely (predicts NONE), also wrong vs gold UNMET but for a different reason (no vocabulary, not mis-polarity)

text: Liam wanted the vault to shut before the guards arrived. The vault shut.
note: flip: same outcome word 'shut' as E-unmet, opposite gold; tests OPEN_CLASS/CLOSE_CLASS opposed pair (new register family)

text: Priya wanted to fill the tank before the trip started. The tank drained.
note: new-family control (FILL_CLASS/EMPTY_CLASS): lexicon OOV on 'drained'/'tank'

text: Priya wanted the tank to drain before the mechanic arrived. The tank drained.
note: flip: same outcome word 'drained' as F-unmet, opposite gold; tests FILL_CLASS/EMPTY_CLASS opposed pair

text: Noah wanted to gather the sheep before the storm broke. The sheep scattered.
note: new-family control (GATHER_CLASS/SCATTER_CLASS): lexicon OOV on 'scattered'/'sheep'

text: Noah wanted the sheep to scatter so the wolf would lose their trail. The sheep scattered.
note: flip: same outcome word 'scattered' as I-unmet, opposite gold; tests GATHER_CLASS/SCATTER_CLASS opposed pair

text: Elena wanted to heal the infected wound before nightfall. The wound worsened.
note: new-family control (HEAL_CLASS/HARM_CLASS): lexicon OOV on 'worsened'/'wound'

text: Elena wanted the wound to worsen so the general would send her home. The wound worsened.
note: flip: same outcome word 'worsened' as J-unmet, opposite gold; tests HEAL_CLASS/HARM_CLASS opposed pair

text: Mara wanted to mend the canoe before the race began. It sank.
note: coverage-stress control: goal object 'canoe' is referred to in the outcome by the PRONOUN 'it', not the verbatim head noun; gold UNMET happens to coincide with the mechanism's referent-mismatch(canoe!=it) fallback regardless of whether pronoun coref actually resolved -- NOT a decisive test on its own

text: Mara wanted the canoe to sink so she could file the insurance claim. It sank.
note: DECISIVE coverage-stress flip: same pronoun-referent setup as K-unmet but gold is MET; a mechanism that (correctly) resolves 'it'->canoe should say MET, a mechanism using naive literal-string referent match will (incorrectly) say UNMET via referent_mismatch(canoe!=it)

text: Grace wanted to mend the ferry before the storm hit. The vessel sank.
note: coverage-stress control: goal object 'ferry' is referred to in the outcome by the SYNONYM/hypernym 'vessel'; gold UNMET happens to coincide with the referent-mismatch(ferry!=vessel) fallback regardless of whether synonym matching actually resolved -- NOT decisive alone

text: Grace wanted the ferry to sink so the insurers would pay out. The vessel sank.
note: DECISIVE coverage-stress flip: same synonym-referent setup as L-unmet but gold is MET; naive literal-string referent match will (incorrectly) say UNMET via referent_mismatch(ferry!=vessel)

text: Diego wanted to save the vintage car from the flood. The garage flooded and the car sank.
note: coverage-stress control: outcome sentence has TWO clauses/objects (garage, car); the mechanism's first-verb-class-match scan binds to the DISTRACTOR 'garage' (from 'flooded') instead of the goal-relevant 'car' (from 'sank'); gold UNMET happens to coincide with the resulting referent-mismatch(car!=garage) regardless -- NOT decisive alone

text: Diego wanted the old shed to collapse so the insurance would cover a rebuild. The workshop flooded and the shed collapsed.
note: DECISIVE multi-object coverage-stress flip: goal-relevant clause ('the shed collapsed') is the SECOND clause; an earlier distractor clause ('the workshop flooded') shares the same broad result-verb-class family and is scanned first, hijacking referent extraction to 'workshop' instead of 'shed' -- naive first-match scanning will (incorrectly) say UNMET via referent_mismatch(shed!=workshop) when gold is MET

text: Derek wanted to fix his bicycle before the race. The library closed early.
note: outcome does not concern the goal's theme (bicycle) at all; mechanism must ABSTAIN, not hallucinate a verdict (abstain path: no recognized result-verb-class token found in the outcome sentence)

text: Farah wanted to open the greenhouse before the frost came. The gardener reached the market.
note: second precision-guard path, distinct from H: the outcome DOES contain a recognized result-verb-class token ('reached', ARRIVE_SUCCEED) but that class is UNRELATED (not same, not opposed) to the goal's OPEN_CLASS -- mechanism must ABSTAIN via verb_class_unrelated, not force a verdict

text: Sara wanted to reach the summit by noon. Sara reached the summit.
note: positive control: non-flip, easy case, both lexicon and mechanism should agree; regression guard

text: Mateo wanted to gather the herd before nightfall. The herd gathered.
note: second positive control on a NEW verb-class family (GATHER_CLASS); non-flip, easy case for the mechanism -- lexicon is expected to be OOV here (no vocabulary for 'gathered'), an honest, reportable capability gap, not a design flaw
